newsitem.title: UK: European firms launch rival Whessoe bid.
newsitem.headline: European firms launch rival Whessoe bid.

text.p: Two European technology firms on Wednesday launched a 52.6 million stg takeover bid for UK-based instruments and controls firm Whessoe plc, in an attempt to trump a 46 million stg agreed offer launched by British controls giant Siebe Plc two weeks ago.
The two partners, Norway's Seatex ASA and Swiss-based Endress+Hauser, said their offer represented a 12.9 percent premium to Siebe's cash offer.
The pair had already agreed to buy 3.14 million Whessoe shares representing about 10.6 percent of its share capital.

Navia and Endress + Hauser said they had approached Whessoe jointly earlier this month in a move which had its roots in a failed attempt in November 1995 by Seatex to purchase Whessoe's main marine instruments and fire security unit Autronica.
"Discussions continued with Whessoe up to Feburary 12, 1997 when Siebe announced its recommended cash offer of 155 pence per Whessoe share," the firms added in their statement.

They said their 175 pence cash offer price also gave a premium of 15.7 percent to Siebe's share alternative offer, and reflected a premium of 94.4 percent on the closing market price of Whessoe shares on February 11, before Siebe's bid emerged.

"Upon successful completion of the offer, it is intended that Navia will acquire (Norway-based) Autronica... Endress + Hauser will acquire Whessoe's other businesses, principally Whessoe's liquid measurement and control division and Elcon Instruments Srl," the bidders added.
